What the model knows, and what it guesses

  • The shape of the dent at a given depth was checked on presses the model never saw, both flush with the dotted face: at the centre down to 38 mm (1.2 mm RMS error over all 105 dots) and 30 mm left of it down to 32 mm. Everywhere else on the top is the same model's prediction, solved every 10 mm; left and right, and front and back, are mirror images.
  • Set back from the dotted face, the weight hardly moves it: 10 mm back, 5 kg moves the face 2.8 mm at most instead of 7.6 mm. That is why every press was filmed flush with the face.
  • How far a weight sinks rests on the stiffness, E = 185 kPa, fitted to dead weights of 1 to 2.4 kg on a pad over the whole top. Each weight alone gave 101 to 190 kPa, and E also leans on parts of the model the dots could not pin down, so read the force behind any sink as good to a factor of 2 to 3.
  • Past about 4.7 kg the pressure under the base passes 12.9 kPa, the cells start to buckle and each extra kilogram sinks further. Nothing that heavy was filmed.
  • Over time, 16% of the stiffness relaxes with a 0.56 s time constant, so a weight keeps sinking for a second or two, and a dent fades the same way after it is lifted. The weight's own bounce is left out: it presses with its full weight, ramped in over 0.15 s.
  • Colour is how far each point of the surface has moved. The black dots are the 105 dots painted on the filmed face.
